summary: Australia reached the Davis Cup final in Malaga with a 2-0 semi-final win over Finland, thanks to straight-sets singles wins by Alexei Popyrin and Alex de Minaur. They will face Italy, who beat Serbia after Jannik Sinner saved three match points to beat Novak Djokovic in singles and then won the doubles. Australia, led by captain Lleyton Hewitt, seeks its first title in 20 years after losing last year's final to Canada.
one_line: Popyrin and de Minaur beat Finland to send Australia into the Davis Cup final against Italy, who ousted Serbia via Sinner's double win over Djokovic.
key_facts: Alexei Popyrin beat Finland's Otto Virtanen 7-6 (7-5), 6-2 in the Davis Cup semi-final, making 11 unforced errors to his opponent's 25.
Alex de Minaur sealed Australia's 2-0 semi-final win over Finland by beating Emil Ruusuvuori 6-4, 6-3, his 11th victory in his last 13 cup singles matches.
Popyrin called his win over Virtanen "probably the biggest win of my career" and said he felt nerves he had never experienced before.
Australia lost last year's Davis Cup final 2-0 to Canada; this is its 49th final and it seeks a 29th title, its first in 20 years.
Australia reached the final by eliminating the Czech Republic and Finland, neither with a top-30 singles player; de Minaur beat Jiri Lehecka in a comeback win in the quarter-final.
Jannik Sinner saved three match points to beat Novak Djokovic 6-2, 2-6, 7-5 in the semi-final, then teamed with Lorenzo Sonego to win the doubles 6-3, 6-4 over Djokovic and Miomir Kecmanovic.
Djokovic was beaten from match-point up for only the fourth time in his career, and his 21-match singles winning streak in the Davis Cup ended.
Sinner, 22, is the first man since Daniil Medvedev in 2019 to beat Djokovic twice in the same year; he also beat him at the ATP Finals six days earlier.
Kecmanovic beat Lorenzo Musetti 6-7 (7-9), 6-2, 6-1 in the opening singles of the Italy-Serbia tie.
The Italy tie finished at 8.15pm after a noon start, while Australia had a day of rest.
The final starts at 2am AEDT on Monday and will be broadcast on 9GEM.
Max Purcell and Matt Ebden, 2022 Wimbledon doubles champions, are Australia's doubles pairing and were not needed against Finland.
